title: `BatchParam` scalar shortcuts test `≈ 0` and `≈ 1`, dropping factors, derivatives and knobs
summary: Arithmetic between a scalar and an array-backed `BatchParam` (addition, subtraction, multiplication and batch/scalar division) takes shortcuts when the scalar is approximately 0 or 1, discarding derivatives and power-series terms. ForwardDiff multipliers at 1 lose their derivatives, zero cases depend on the signs of the zero and the derivative, and GTPSA series with scalar part 0 or 1 lose their nonconstant coefficients. For a 0.5 m quadrupole with `Kn1 = s * BatchParam([0.3, 0.6])` and initial x = 1 mm, dx/ds at s = 1 is [0, 0] instead of [−1.833×10⁻⁴, −3.583×10⁻⁴] m, which scalar tracking and finite differences recover. Float64 factors within a relative 1.490×10⁻⁸ of 1 and Float32 factors within 3.453×10⁻⁴ are ignored, and division by zero gives +∞ in every lane.

title: Simultaneous magnetic-strength convention changes rescale the partner twice
summary: A magnetic strength can be set as a field (B) or normalized to rigidity (K), integrated or per unit length. Reassigning a nonzero strength its current value through a name that changes both choices at once rescales the unassigned normal or skew partner by an extra L or 1/L, where L is the element length; this self-assignment must preserve the field, as two successive single-change self-assignments do. For a proton dipole with L = 0.25 m, rigidity R = 7.3 T·m, `Bn0` = −0.21 T and `Bs0` = 0.13 T, assigning `Kn0L` its own value keeps the kick Δpx = 7.192×10⁻³ but reduces Δpy from 4.452×10⁻³, the uniform-field Lorentz-force value, to 1.113×10⁻³. A zero partner or L = 1 m hides the error.
